```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("rvis-setup.R")
```

rvis table wrappers show a data frame as an interactive html table: sortable and searchable
(DT), filterable and editable with cell graphics (TFD3, D3TableFilter), or reshaped by the
reader (pivot). Examples are evaluated when the package of the wrapper is installed; otherwise
only their code is shown.

## Data: violent crime rates by US state (`USArrests`)

`USArrests` gives arrests per 100,000 residents for assault, murder and rape in each US state
in 1973, and the percent of the population living in urban areas. `state.region` adds the
region of each state.

```{r data}
arrests <- data.frame(USArrests, region = as.character(state.region))
head(arrests)
```

## Tables {#table}

The `label` dimension selects the columns to show (all columns by default). Row names are
shown when `config$withRowNames` is `TRUE`.

### DT

```{r, eval=has_plotter("DT")}
rvisPlot(type = "table", plotter = "DT", obj = arrests,
         config = list(paging.length = 5))
```

### TFD3 (embedded in rvis)

TFD3 tables have a filter row (try `>10` in the Murder column) and can turn cells into
graphics with `config$column.shape` and colour columns with `config$column.color`.

```{r}
rvisPlot(type = "table", plotter = "TFD3", obj = arrests,
         label = list("Murder", "Assault", "UrbanPop", "region"),
         config = list(column.shape = list(Assault = "bar"),
                       column.color = list(UrbanPop = c("white", "steelblue")),
                       column.footer = list(Murder = mean, Assault = mean),
                       height = 400))
```

### D3TableFilter

`D3TableFilter` is the published version of the TFD3 widget and takes the same settings.

```{r, eval=has_plotter("D3TableFilter")}
rvisPlot(type = "table", plotter = "D3TableFilter", obj = arrests,
         config = list(column.shape = list(Murder = "bubble")))
```

## Tables from a long table {#table-molten}

### TFD3

```{r}
rvisPlot(type = "table.molten", plotter = "TFD3", obj = arrests, label = list("region", "Murder", "Assault"))
```

## Pivot tables

A pivot table lets the reader drag columns into rows and columns and choose how values are
aggregated and shown (table, heat map, charts).

### pivot

```{r, eval=has_plotter("rpivotTable")}
rvisPlot(type = "table", plotter = "pivot", obj = arrests, rows = "region",
         vals = "Murder", aggregatorName = "Average", rendererName = "Heatmap")
```

## Legacy table function {#Table}

`DT.Table()` is an older function kept for backward compatibility: it takes the table as `x`
and DataTables `options` directly.

```{r, eval=has_plotter("DT")}
DT.Table(arrests, options = list(pageLength = 5))
```
